name: Jasperlode Mine
summary: In north-central Elwynn, kobolds and giant spiders hold Jasperlode Mine. Its shafts once sent iron and minerals to Stormwind City, but the kingdom lacks the strength to reclaim them.

sections.title: A Lost Resource in Elwynn
sections.body: Jasperlode Mine once sent a steady supply of minerals to Stormwind, as did nearby Fargodeep. Now the kingdom's forces are stretched thin by threats beyond its borders and unrest at home. Local garrisons cannot guard the shafts. Kobolds drove out the human miners and seized the mine, hoarding stolen gold and tallow candles.

sections.title: Dangers in the Deep
sections.body: Mine spiders have made their home beneath Jasperlode Mine's timber supports. A massive matriarch called Mother Fang leads them. They prey on kobolds who trespass and on unwary prospectors. Salvaging the mine means facing those dangers in its depths.

faq.answer: Stormwind's army is spread thin across the realm, leaving rural outposts like Goldshire short on manpower. Once the human miners lost their guards, kobolds swarmed the dig sites.

faq.q: What is the difference between Jasperlode and Fargodeep?
faq.answer: Fargodeep Mine lies south near the Maclure and Stonefield farms. Jasperlode sits north in the foothills near the river. Kobolds hold both major Elwynn mineral sites.

faq.q: What lurks in the back of the mine?
faq.answer: Predatory mine spiders lurk in the deepest shafts, led by a massive arachnid called Mother Fang. Even the kobolds avoid their webbed caverns.

faq.q: Why hasn't Marshal Dughan cleared the mine?
faq.answer: Marshal Dughan lacks the troops for a prolonged clearing underground. He must cover Defias river patrols, gnoll incursions, and garrison duties, so the local militia relies on traveling adventurers to scout the mine and cull its threats.

angles.text: Jasperlode's mineral veins draw prospectors willing to face kobold pickaxes and spider webs to stake a claim.
Stormwind needs Jasperlode's raw metal to maintain its equipment supplies while the kingdom's borders face constant peril.
